source_text:
Ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ καὶ μέτρον ἐπιστολῆς ἐκφεύγει τὸ περὶ τούτων λεπτολογεῖν καὶ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀγάπην
ἐπιστεύσαμεν ἀρκεσθή σεσθαι τῷ κεφαλαίῳ τῆς ἡμετέρας ἐκθέσεως καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ προσθήσειν οἴκοθεν–∆ίδου γάρ, φησί, σοφῷ ἀφορμὴν καὶ σοφώτε ρος ἔσται–, καὶ ταῦτα ἀποχρώντως γεγραφέναι νομίζομεν. Οἷς ἀρκεῖ βραχεῖαν προσθεῖναι παράκλησιν. Παρακαλοῦμεν γὰρ μένειν ὑμᾶς υἱοὺς εἰρήνης, ἵνα πληρώσητε τὴν ἀποστολικὴν ἐντολήν, σύμψυχοι τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες καὶ τῶν παθημάτων τῶν ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ κεκοινωνηκότες. Μὴ δῶτε τῷ πονηρῷ διαζεῦξαι τὰ καλῶς συνημμένα μήτε τοῖς λύκοις ἑαυτοὺς εὐαλωτοτέρους ποιήσητε τῇ διχοστασίᾳ τὰς ἐκείνων βεβαιοῦντες εὐχάς. Ἐμάθο μεν γὰρ ὅσους ἄθλους ὑπὲρ τῆς ὀρθοδοξίας ὑπέστητε. Τὰς οὖν ἀπειλὰς καὶ τὰς ἀνάγκας τὰς παρὰ τῶν ὑπεναντίων νικήσαντες μηδένα δῶτε διαστάσει καιρόν, μήποτε κατὰ βραχὺ παρεισρυό μενον μῖσος, ἐὰν σχῇ τόπον, μεγάλους ὑμῖν κρημνοὺς ὑποθήσῃ. Ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν ταῖς δοξολογίαις τὸ πνεῦμα πατρὶ καὶ υἱῷ χρὴ συνδοξάζειν καὶ εἰδέναι τοῦτο, ὅτι οἱ τὴν ἀσυγχώρητον ἁμαρτίαν διὰ τῆς εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα βλασφημίας ἐξαμαρτάνοντες εἰκῆ παραι τοῦνται τὴν πρὸς τοὺς Ἀρειανοὺς κοινωνίαν. Μετὰ γὰρ ἐκείνων κατακριθήσονται. Εὐχόμεθα δὲ ὑμᾶς ἄτμητον τὸ σῶμα τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἀφιλονείκως φυλάξαντας, εἰρηνικῶς μὲν ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι τὸν λειπόμενον διάγειν χρόνον, ἐνδόξως δὲ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τῆς κρίσεως παραστῆναι τῷ τοῦ Χριστοῦ βήματι.
thought_title: Closing exhortation to peace and right glorification of the Spirit
orientation: Amphilochius is closing his synodal letter, having just affirmed the Trinity and the Spirit's place in the Godhead.
pass_a_gloss: But since both the measure of a letter escapes the fine-detail discussion about these things and we trusted your love to be satisfied with the main point of our exposition and to add the rest from your own resources—for, it says, give a wise man an opportunity and he will be wiser—, we consider these things to have been written sufficiently. To these things it is enough to add a brief exhortation. For we exhort you to remain sons of peace, in order that you may fulfill the apostolic command, being of one soul, thinking the one thing, and having shared in the sufferings for Christ. Do not give the evil one an opportunity to separate what has been well joined, nor make yourselves more easily caught by the wolves, confirming their prayers by division. For we have learned how many contests you endured for orthodoxy. Therefore, having conquered the threats and the constraints from the adversaries, give no opportunity to division, lest hatred creeping in little by little, if it has a place, may set great cliffs under you. But also in the doxologies it is necessary to glorify the Spirit together with the Father and the Son, and to know this, that those who commit the unforgivable sin through blasphemy against the Spirit vainly reject communion with the Arians. For with those they will be condemned. And we pray that you, having kept the body of the church uncut without quarreling, may pass the remaining time peacefully in the present age, and may stand gloriously before the judgment seat of Christ on the day of judgment.

lemmas.gloss: of one soul, united in spirit

choices.term: ἀρκεσθήσεσθαι τῷ κεφαλαίῳ τῆς ἡμετέρας ἐκθέσεως
choices.english: to be satisfied with the main point of our exposition
choices.why: κεφάλαιον here means the summary or main point, not a chapter heading; the literal sense is that the recipients will be content with the condensed statement
rejected: to be content with the chapter of our statement
to be satisfied with the head of our exposition

choices.term: ∆ίδου γάρ, φησί, σοφῷ ἀφορμὴν καὶ σοφώτερος ἔσται
choices.english: for, it says, give a wise man an opportunity and he will be wiser
choices.why: This is a proverbial saying introduced by φησί; the literal rendering preserves the imperative and the comparative
rejected: give a wise man a starting point and he will become wiser
offer a wise man an occasion and he will be more wise

choices.why: The Semitic idiom 'sons of peace' is kept literally to preserve the biblical resonance

choices.english: being of one soul, thinking the one thing
choices.why: σύμψυχοι is a compound adjective meaning sharing one soul; the participle φρονοῦντες with τὸ ἕν is rendered literally to keep the Pauline echo
rejected: united in spirit, having one mind
of one accord, thinking the same thing

choices.why: καιρός here means opportunity or occasion, not time; the dative διαστάσει is the recipient of the opportunity

choices.english: may set great cliffs under you
choices.why: κρημνός means a steep cliff or precipice; the metaphor of undermining or setting a trap is kept literal
rejected: may place great precipices beneath you
may lay great snares for you

bible_refs.note: σύμψυχοι τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες echoes Paul's exhortation to be of one mind
τῶν παθημάτων τῶν ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ κεκοινωνηκότες echoes sharing in Christ's sufferings
τὸ πνεῦμα πατρὶ καὶ υἱῷ χρὴ συνδοξάζειν reflects the baptismal command naming Father, Son, and Holy Spirit

pass_b_english: But since discussing these matters in fine detail would exceed the measure of a letter, and since we have trusted that your love will be satisfied with the main point of our exposition and will add the rest from your own resources—for, as the saying goes, give a wise man an opportunity and he will be wiser—we consider what we have written to be sufficient. To this it is enough to add a brief exhortation.

We urge you to remain sons of peace, so that you may fulfill the apostolic command, being of one soul, thinking the one thing, and sharing in the sufferings endured for Christ. Do not give the evil one a chance to separate what has been well joined together, and do not make yourselves easier prey for the wolves by division, thereby confirming their prayers. For we have learned how many struggles you have undergone for the sake of orthodoxy.

Since you have overcome the threats and the pressures from your adversaries, give no opportunity to division, lest hatred creeping in little by little, if it finds a place, may set great cliffs under you. But in your doxologies you must glorify the Spirit together with the Father and the Son, and know this: those who, through blasphemy against the Spirit, incur the unforgivable sin vainly reject communion with the Arians. For they will be condemned with them.

We pray that you, having kept the body of the church uncut and without quarreling, may pass the remaining time in this present age peacefully, and may stand gloriously before the judgment seat of Christ on the day of judgment.

problems.quote: those who commit the unforgivable sin through blasphemy against the Spirit vainly reject communion with the Arians
problems.source_quote: οἱ τὴν ἀσυγχώρητον ἁμαρτίαν διὰ τῆς εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα βλασφημίας ἐξαμαρτάνοντες εἰκῆ παραι τοῦνται τὴν πρὸς τοὺς Ἀρειανοὺς κοινωνίαν
problems.why: Greek says they are rightly excluded from communion with the Arians, not that they reject it.
problems.fix: those who, through blasphemy against the Spirit, incur the unforgivable sin are rightly excluded from communion with the Arians
problems.ruling: παραιτοῦνται means 'refuse/reject,' but context and logic show they are excluded, not rejecting; εἰκῆ ('in vain') confirms the action is futile, implying forced exclusion.

edits.old: those who commit the unforgivable sin through blasphemy against the Spirit vainly reject communion with the Arians
edits.new: those who, through blasphemy against the Spirit, incur the unforgivable sin are rightly excluded from communion with the Arians

fixed: Corrected mistranslation: Greek παραιτοῦνται means 'are excluded/renounced' (passive sense), not 'reject'; the Arians exclude them, so they are rightly excluded from communion with the Arians.

problems.quote: are rightly excluded from communion with the Arians
problems.source_quote: εἰκῆ παραιτοῦνται τὴν πρὸς τοὺς Ἀρειανοὺς κοινωνίαν
problems.why: εἰκῆ means 'in vain,' not 'rightly'; παραιτοῦνται means 'reject/refuse,' not 'are excluded from'
problems.fix: vainly reject communion with the Arians
problems.ruling: εἰκῆ = 'in vain', παραιτοῦνται = 'they vainly beg', not 'rightly excluded'

problems.quote: are rightly excluded from communion with the Arians
problems.source_quote: εἰκῆ παραιτοῦνται τὴν πρὸς τοὺς Ἀρειανοὺς κοινωνίαν
problems.why: εἰκῆ = 'in vain' mistranslated as 'rightly'; παραιτοῦνται = 'reject/refuse' mistranslated as 'are excluded'
problems.fix: vainly reject communion with the Arians
problems.ruling: Same phrase: εἰκῆ παραιτοῦνται = 'they vainly request', not 'are excluded'

edits.old: are rightly excluded from communion with the Arians
edits.new: vainly reject communion with the Arians

fixed: Source: εἰκῆ παραιτοῦνται τὴν πρὸς τοὺς Ἀρειανοὺς κοινωνίαν. εἰκῆ means 'in vain,' not 'rightly,' and παραιτοῦνται means 'reject/refuse,' not 'are excluded from.' The English misstates the source, so I corrected it to 'vainly reject communion with the Arians.'

problems.quote: the persons and hypostases are shown to be three
problems.why: Intro says 'person' singular for each reality; text uses 'persons' plural for the three together. Reader may not connect these.
problems.fix: Clarify in intro that 'person' = each, 'persons' = all three.

problems.quote: lest hatred creeping in little by little, if it finds a place, may set great cliffs under you
problems.why: 'Set great cliffs under you' is nonsensical English; likely means 'cause great rifts/division' or 'undermine with cliffs'.
problems.fix: Revise to 'may open great chasms beneath you' or similar.

problems.why: Same group described differently; reader may not connect them.
problems.fix: Use one label, e.g., 'opponents of the Spirit,' in both places.

variants.text: those who, through blasphemy against the Spirit, incur the unforgivable sin

problems.quote: those who, through blasphemy against the Spirit, incur the unforgivable sin vainly reject communion with the Arians. For they will be condemned with them.
problems.why: Unclear whether 'they' refers to the blasphemers or the Arians in the final sentence.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'For the blasphemers will be condemned with the Arians.'

problems.quote: may set great cliffs under you
problems.why: Probably a mistranslation of a metaphor for undermining or causing ruin.
problems.fix: Rephrase as 'may undermine your foundations' or 'may bring ruin upon you.'

edits.old: may set great cliffs under you
edits.new: may open great chasms beneath you

edits.old: For they will be condemned with them.
edits.new: For the blasphemers will be condemned with the Arians.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'persons' vs 'person' is a brief-level concern, not an error in this English text; no edit made.
The phrase 'set great cliffs under you' is indeed nonsensical English for the Greek κρημνοὺς ὑποθήσῃ; revised to 'open great chasms beneath you'.
The glossary issue about 'opponents of the Spirit' is a brief-level concern; the English uses the glossary term correctly.
The referent of 'they' in the final sentence is ambiguous; clarified to 'the blasphemers' and 'the Arians'.
The mistranslation of the cliffs metaphor is fixed by the same edit as above.

problems.why: Wolves' prayers? Unclear whether 'their' refers to wolves (heretics) or divisions; context suggests heretics pray for church division, but 'confirming their prayers' is awkward.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'granting what they pray for' or 'fulfilling their wishes'.

problems.why: Biblical allusion to Philippians 2:2, but 'the one thing' is archaic; modern readers may stumble.
problems.fix: 'thinking the same thing' or note as biblical quotation.

edits.new: thereby granting what they pray for

fixed: Source: βεβαιοῦντες εὐχάς. 'Confirming their prayers' is awkward and unclear; 'granting what they pray for' clarifies that the wolves' prayers are fulfilled by division.
Source: τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες. 'The one thing' is archaic; 'the same thing' is clearer and still faithful to the source.

last_rejected.why: 'εὐχάς' here means 'wishes/desires' (of the wolves), not 'prayers' in religious sense; wolves don't pray.
last_rejected.ruling: εὐχὰς can mean prayers or wishes; translation conveys intent, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: 'κρημνοὺς' means 'precipices'/'chasms' as dangers, but 'set cliffs under you' is nonsensical; should be 'lay great pitfalls' or 'open great chasms beneath you'.
last_rejected.ruling: κρημνοὺς = cliffs/precipices; literal phrasing is odd but meaning of danger is retained.

last_rejected.why: 'ἐξαμαρτάνοντες' means 'committing/sinning', not 'incurring'; they actively commit the sin through blasphemy.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐξαμαρτάνοντες = committing sin; “incur” is a close synonym, no loss of meaning.

last_rejected.why: 'ἀφιλονείκως' means 'without contention/strife', adverb modifying 'having kept'; 'without quarreling' is close but 'uncut and without strife' better. Minor issue.

last_rejected.quote: pass the remaining time in this present age peacefully
last_rejected.source_quote: εἰρηνικῶς μὲν ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι τὸν λειπόμενον διάγειν χρόνον
last_rejected.why: 'εἰρηνικῶς' goes with 'stand before' too? No, it's paired with 'ἐνδόξως'; 'peacefully... gloriously'. But 'pass... peacefully' is fine. Actually checking: 'ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι' modifies 'διάγειν', 'in the present age'. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰρηνικῶς … τὸν λειπόμενον διάγειν χρόνον = pass remaining time peacefully; translation accurate.
